name: Self-Esteem Issues
description: Persistent patterns of low self-worth, self-criticism, imposter syndrome, or difficulty recognising your own value that can hold you back from taking risks, setting boundaries, and living fully.

immediateActions.title: Catch the Critic & Rewrite
instructions: Write down the exact self-critical thought that's loudest right now
Now write: WHO does this voice sound like? A parent? Teacher? Former bully? Your own voice?
Ask: Would I say this exact sentence to a friend I love? The answer is almost always NO
Rewrite the thought as what you WOULD say to that friend — be generous and warm
Write the kind version 3 times out loud or in your head
Place your hand on your heart for 15 seconds and take 3 breaths, breathing in the kind version

immediateActions.title: 3 Wins (Even Tiny)
instructions: Write down 3 wins, achievements, or moments you handled well — they can be micro
Examples: I got out of bed today, I drank water, I responded to that message, I was kind to someone
For each win, write one sentence about why it counts and one about what it shows about you
Example: I tried today shows I am persistent even when it's hard
Read all three out loud and pause for 5 seconds on each, letting it land

immediateActions.title: Self-Compassion Break (3 Phrases)
instructions: Say out loud or silently: This is a moment of suffering.
Say: Suffering is part of life. I am not alone in this.
Say: May I be kind to myself.
Now say: May I give myself the compassion I need.
Place both hands over your heart and breathe warmth into that area for 30 seconds
Notice what shifts in your body after this — not fixing, just allowing

tools.name: Evidence Journal
tools.description: Gather concrete evidence that contradicts your inner critic — wins, kind acts, moments of growth.

tools.name: Self-Compassion Letter Builder
tools.description: Guided letter templates for writing compassionate letters to yourself from different perspectives.

tools.name: Inner Critic Workbook
tools.description: Worksheets to identify critic patterns, origins, and create an inner ally alternative voice.

tools.name: Values & Strengths Card Sort
tools.description: Interactive card sort to discover your core values and character strengths you may be overlooking.

tools.name: Boundaries as Self-Respect Builder
tools.description: Learn how to set small boundaries as acts of self-respect with scripts and practice prompts.

safetyGuidance: Low self-esteem is usually learned, not the truth about you — it can be unlearned with intentional practice and often responds well to therapy approaches like CBT, ACT, and compassion-focused therapy. If persistent low self-worth is accompanied by self-critical thoughts of hopelessness, speaking with a therapist can help you reconnect to yourself the kindness you so freely give others. You are worthy of your own kindness, not the version of yourself; worthiness is not earned, it is your birthright.
